import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Implicit graph conjecture

The implicit graph conjecture asked whether every hereditary family of graphs of at most
factorial speed has an efficient implicit representation. It was refuted by Hatami and Hatami.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Implicit graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/implicit_graph_conjecture)
- [Hatami and Hatami, *The Implicit Graph Conjecture is False*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13198)
-/

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

/-- A family of labeled finite graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking induced
subgraphs. Taking `m = n` also makes it closed under relabeling by graph isomorphisms. -/
def IsHereditary (F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ {m n : ℕ} (f : Fin m ↪ Fin n) {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}, G ∈ F n → G.comap f ∈ F m

/-- A family has at most factorial speed if the number of its labeled `n`-vertex graphs is at
most `2 ^ (C * n * log₂ n)` for one constant `C` independent of `n`. -/
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, (F n).ncard ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Nat.log 2 n)

/-- A graph family has an efficient implicit representation if one decoder works for every graph
in the family, using injective binary vertex labels of at most `C * log₂ n` bits. No
computability condition is imposed on the decoder. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation
    (F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℕ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Bool),
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ F n →
      ∃ label : Fin n → List Bool, Function.Injective label ∧
        (∀ v, (label v).length ≤ C * Nat.log 2 n) ∧
        ∀ u v, D (label u) (label v) = true ↔ G.Adj u v

/--
**Implicit graph conjecture.** Every hereditary graph family with at most factorial speed of
growth (at most $2^{O(n\log n)}$ labeled graphs on $n$ vertices) was conjectured to admit an
efficient implicit representation: one decoder, depending only on the family, should determine
adjacency from injective vertex labels of $O(\log n)$ bits. The decoder is not required to be
computable. Hatami and Hatami refuted the conjecture, so its answer is false.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      IsHereditary F → HasAtMostFactorialSpeed F → HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by
  sorry

end ImplicitGraphConjecture
modeling_decisions: Represented a graph family as `F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`, matching the source's labeled graphs on `[n]` and making the speed count unambiguous.

Defined heredity by pullback (`SimpleGraph.comap`) along every injection `Fin m ↪ Fin n`. This is exactly the injection-based formulation in Hatami–Hatami and includes closure under isomorphism when `m = n`.

Rendered `2^{O(n log n)}` as the existence of a uniform natural constant `C` with `(F n).ncard ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Nat.log 2 n)` for every `n`. The small cases `n = 0, 1` cause no distortion because there is at most one labeled simple graph in each case.
Rendered `O(log n)` labels as binary lists of length at most `C * Nat.log 2 n`, with a single constant and decoder chosen for the whole family before quantifying over sizes and graphs.
Required vertex labels to be injective, matching Wikipedia's terminology of vertex identifiers and the stated equivalence with induced-universal graphs of polynomial size.
Used an unrestricted function `List Bool → List Bool → Bool` as decoder, deliberately imposing no computability or complexity condition, as in Hatami–Hatami's formulation.
Recorded the theorem as `research solved` with `answer(False)`, following the decomposition's correction based on the Hatami–Hatami refutation despite the list entry's stale open status.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The implicit graph conjecture

An *efficient implicit representation* (or *adjacency labeling scheme*) of an $n$-vertex graph
$G$ in a family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs assigns to each vertex of $G$ a binary code of length
$O(\log n)$ so that the adjacency of every pair of vertices is determined by a *decoder*
function of their two codes. The decoder may depend on $\mathcal{F}$ but not on the individual
graph $G$. A counting argument shows that a family admitting such a representation contains at
most $2^{O(n \log n)}$ labeled graphs on $n$ vertices, i.e. it has *at most factorial speed of
growth*.

Kannan, Naor and Rudich asked whether, conversely, every *hereditary* family (closed under taking
induced subgraphs, equivalently defined by forbidden induced subgraphs) with at most factorial
speed of growth admits an efficient implicit representation. Spinrad restated this as the
**implicit graph conjecture**. It was refuted by Hatami and Hatami, who constructed, for every
$\delta > 0$, a hereditary family of at most factorial speed all of whose implicit
representations need codes of length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$.

A family of finite labeled graphs is modelled below as `F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`,
where `F n` is the set of members of the family with vertex set `Fin n` (the $n$-vertex labeled
graphs $\mathcal{F}_n$ of [HH22]).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Implicit graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/implicit_graph_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KNR92] Kannan, S., Naor, M. and Rudich, S., *Implicit representation of graphs*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992), 596–603.
- [Sp03] Spinrad, J. P., *Efficient graph representations*. Fields Institute Monographs 19,
  AMS (2003).
- [HH22] Hatami, H. and Hatami, P., *The implicit graph conjecture is false*.
  FOCS 2022, [arXiv:2111.13198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13198).
-/

open Filter

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

/-- A graph family `F` is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: for
every injection `σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n` and every `G ∈ F n`, the graph on `Fin m` in which `i` and
`j` are adjacent exactly when `σ i` and `σ j` are adjacent in `G` (that is, `G.comap σ`) belongs
to `F m`. Taking `m = n` shows that a hereditary family is also closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsHereditary (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄ (σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.comap σ ∈ F m

/-- A graph family `F` has *at most factorial speed of growth* if the number of labeled
`n`-vertex graphs in the family satisfies $|\mathcal{F}_n| \le 2^{O(n \log n)}$. -/
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)

/-- A graph family `F` has an *efficient implicit representation* if there are a constant `C` and
a decoder `D` on pairs of binary codes, both depending only on `F`, such that every `n`-vertex
graph `G ∈ F n` admits an assignment `ℓ` of binary codes of length at most `C * log₂ n` to its
vertices with `u` and `v` adjacent in `G` exactly when `D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)` holds.

Following [HH22], the decoder is not required to be computable. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℕ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Prop), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ F n,
    ∃ ℓ : Fin n → List Bool,
      (∀ v, (ℓ v).length ≤ C * Nat.log 2 n) ∧ ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)

/--
The **implicit graph conjecture** (posed as a question by Kannan, Naor and Rudich [KNR92] and
stated as a conjecture by Spinrad [Sp03]): does every hereditary family of graphs with at most
factorial speed of growth (at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$ labeled graphs on $n$ vertices) admit an
efficient implicit representation, i.e. an adjacency labeling scheme with $O(\log n)$-bit labels
(equivalently, induced-universal graphs of polynomial size)?

The answer is no: Hatami and Hatami [HH22] showed that for every $\delta > 0$ there is a
hereditary family of at most factorial speed whose implicit representations need codes of length
$\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 68]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      IsHereditary F → HasAtMostFactorialSpeed F → HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by
  sorry

/-- The family of all graphs is hereditary. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isHereditary_univ : IsHereditary fun n => (Set.univ : Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

/-- The family of edgeless graphs is hereditary. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isHereditary_bot : IsHereditary fun n => ({⊥} : Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) := by
  rintro m n σ G rfl
  simp

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has at most factorial speed of growth. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasAtMostFactorialSpeed_bot :
    HasAtMostFactorialSpeed fun n => ({⊥} : Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) :=
  ⟨0, Eventually.of_forall fun n => by simp⟩

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has an efficient implicit representation: use empty codes and
the decoder that never accepts. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasEfficientImplicitRepresentation_bot :
    HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation fun n => ({⊥} : Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) :=
  ⟨0, fun _ _ => False, fun n G hG => ⟨fun _ => [], fun _ => by simp, fun u v => by
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG
    simp [hG]⟩⟩

end ImplicitGraphConjecture

modeling_decisions: Graph families are modelled as `F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`, i.e. `F n` is the set of labeled n-vertex graphs on vertex set [n], exactly as the 𝓕_n of Hatami–Hatami (arXiv:2111.13198).

At most factorial speed is `∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)`, the literal asymptotic reading of |F_n| ≤ 2^{O(n log n)}. Natural log vs log₂ is absorbed in C; 'eventually' vs 'for all n' is equivalent because |F_0|, |F_1| ≤ 1 and finitely many small n can be absorbed into C.

Efficient implicit representation: `∃ (C : ℕ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Prop), ∀ n, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∃ ℓ : Fin n → List Bool, (∀ v, (ℓ v).length ≤ C * Nat.log 2 n) ∧ ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)`. The constant and decoder are chosen once for the whole family (quantifier order as in the source). The decoder is Prop-valued rather than Bool-valued (classically equivalent) and, following Hatami–Hatami, is NOT required to be polynomial-time computable (the original KNR requirement); their refutation holds regardless, so the truth value is unaffected.

Code length is bounded by ≤ C·⌊log₂ n⌋ for every n (not just eventually) and codes are lists of length at most, not exactly, C log₂ n; labels are not required to be distinct; the adjacency equivalence is required for all pairs u v including u = v (forcing D x x to be false on used codes). Each of these choices is equivalent to the alternatives up to a constant factor in C (pad codes / prefix a vertex index / handle n = 1 with the empty code), so the existence of an O(log n) scheme is unchanged. At n = 1 the bound forces the empty code and D [] [] = False, which is harmless.

Used the `answer(False) ↔ (conjecture)` style rather than `¬ (conjecture)`, since Kannan–Naor–Rudich posed the problem as a question and the decomposition notes request answer(False); category is `research solved` (refuted by Hatami–Hatami, FOCS 2022) despite the Wikipedia list marking it open.

open SimpleGraph

/-- A family of finite labelled graphs: `F n` is the set of members of the family whose vertex
set is `Fin n`, i.e. the $n$-vertex graphs of the family, following [HaHa22]. -/
abbrev GraphFamily : Type := ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

/-- A graph family is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: whenever
`G ∈ F n` and `H` is a graph on `Fin m` isomorphic to an induced subgraph of `G`, then `H ∈ F m`.
Taking `m = n` shows that a hereditary family is closed under isomorphism. Equivalently, the
family is defined by a (possibly infinite) set of forbidden induced subgraphs. -/
def IsHereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin m), H ⊴ G → H ∈ F m

/-- A graph family has *at most factorial speed of growth* if the number of $n$-vertex members
is at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$, i.e. there is a constant $C$ with $|F_n| \le 2^{C n \log n}$
for all $n$. -/

  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)

with $O(\log n)$-bit labels) if there are a constant $C$ and a *decoder*
`D : {0,1}* × {0,1}* → Bool`, both depending only on the family, such that every $n$-vertex
member `G` of the family admits a labeling of its vertices by binary strings of length at most
$C \log n$ from which adjacency is recovered by the decoder: `G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)`.

def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℝ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Bool), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ F n,

  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG ⊢

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

/-- A family of labeled finite simple graphs, indexed by the number of vertices. -/
abbrev GraphFamily := (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

/-- A graph family is hereditary if it is closed under every induced subgraph obtained by an
injection of finite vertex sets. Taking an injection `Fin n ↪ Fin n` also gives closure under
relabeling. -/
def Hereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ {m n : ℕ} (σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n) {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)},
    G ∈ F n → G.comap σ ∈ F m

/-- A graph family has at most factorial speed if the number of its labeled `n`-vertex graphs is
at most `2 ^ (C * n * log₂ n)` for one family-wide constant `C`. -/
def HasFactorialSpeed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, (F n).ncard ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Nat.log 2 n)

/-- A graph family has an efficient implicit representation if there are one constant and one
decoder, fixed for the whole family, such that every vertex of every `n`-vertex member graph can
be assigned a binary string of length at most `C * log₂ n`, from which adjacency is decoded. No
computability condition is imposed on the decoder. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℕ) (decoder : List Bool → List Bool → Bool),
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ F n →
      ∃ label : Fin n → List Bool,
        (∀ v, (label v).length ≤ C * Nat.log 2 n) ∧
        ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ decoder (label u) (label v) = true

/--
The implicit graph conjecture asserted that every hereditary graph family whose number of
labeled `n`-vertex graphs is at most $2^{O(n\log n)}$ has an efficient implicit representation:
there should be a family-wide constant $C$ and decoder such that every member graph admits
vertex labels of at most $C\log_2 n$ bits and adjacency is determined solely from two labels.
The decoder is not required to be computable. Hatami and Hatami disproved this assertion, so the
answer is false.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ F : GraphFamily,
      Hereditary F → HasFactorialSpeed F → HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by
  sorry

end ImplicitGraphConjecture

/-!
# The implicit graph conjecture

An *adjacency labeling scheme* (or *efficient implicit representation*) for a family
$\mathcal F$ of finite graphs consists of a decoder, depending only on $\mathcal F$, such that
the vertices of every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal F$ can be labeled with $O(\log n)$ bits
so that the decoder, applied to the labels of two vertices, tells whether they are adjacent.
A counting argument shows that such a family has at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$ labeled graphs on
$n$ vertices (*at most factorial speed of growth*).

The *implicit graph conjecture* asserts the converse for hereditary families: every family of
graphs that is closed under taking induced subgraphs and has at most factorial speed of growth
admits an adjacency labeling scheme. It was asked as a question by Kannan, Naor and Rudich and
stated as a conjecture by Spinrad.

The conjecture is false: Hatami and Hatami showed that for every $\delta > 0$ there is a
hereditary family of at most factorial speed of growth whose implicit representations require
labels of length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Implicit graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/implicit_graph_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Kannan, M. Naor, S. Rudich, *Implicit representation of graphs*,
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992), 596–603.
- J. P. Spinrad, *Efficient graph representations*, Fields Institute Monographs 19,
  American Mathematical Society, 2003.
- H. Hatami, P. Hatami, *The implicit graph conjecture is false*, FOCS 2022,
  [arXiv:2111.13198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13198)
-/

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

open Asymptotics Filter

/-- A *family of finite graphs*: for each `n`, a set `F n` of labeled graphs on the vertex set
`Fin n`. -/
abbrev GraphFamily := (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

/-- A graph family `F` is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: for every
`G ∈ F n` and every injection `σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n`, the graph on `Fin m` in which `i` and `j`
are adjacent if and only if `σ i` and `σ j` are adjacent in `G` belongs to `F m`. Taking
`m = n` shows that a hereditary family is closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsHereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄ (σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.comap σ ∈ F m

/-- A graph family `F` has *at most factorial speed of growth* if the number of labeled
`n`-vertex graphs in `F` is $2^{O(n \log n)}$, that is, $\log |F_n| = O(n \log n)$. -/
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  (fun n : ℕ => Real.log ((F n).ncard : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) * Real.log n

/-- A graph family `F` has an *efficient implicit representation* (an *adjacency labeling
scheme*) if there are a constant `C` and a decoder `D`, which takes two bitstrings and returns a
truth value, both depending only on `F`, such that every `n`-vertex graph `G ∈ F n` admits a
labeling `ℓ` of its vertices by bitstrings of length at most `C * ⌊log₂ n⌋` with
`G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)` for all vertices `u v`. The decoder is not required to be
computable. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℕ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Prop),
    ∀ n, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∃ ℓ : Fin n → List Bool,
      (∀ v, (ℓ v).length ≤ C * Nat.log 2 n) ∧ ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)

/-- **The implicit graph conjecture** (Kannan–Naor–Rudich, Spinrad): every hereditary family of
finite graphs with at most factorial speed of growth, that is, with at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$
labeled graphs on $n$ vertices, admits an efficient implicit representation, that is, an
adjacency labeling scheme with $O(\log n)$-bit labels and a decoder depending only on the
family.

The conjecture is false: Hatami and Hatami (2022) showed that for every $\delta > 0$ there is a
hereditary family of at most factorial speed of growth whose implicit representations require
labels of length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 68]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ F : GraphFamily, IsHereditary F → HasAtMostFactorialSpeed F →
      HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by

theorem isHereditary_univ : IsHereditary fun _ => Set.univ :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has at most factorial speed of growth. -/

with the empty bitstring and let the decoder always answer "not adjacent". -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasEfficientImplicitRepresentation_bot :
    HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation fun _ => {⊥} := by
  refine ⟨0, fun _ _ => False, fun n G hG => ⟨fun _ => [], fun _ => by simp, fun u v => ?_⟩⟩
  simp_all

end ImplicitGraphConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The implicit graph conjecture

An *implicit representation* (or *adjacency labeling scheme*) of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ in a
family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs assigns a binary code to each vertex of $G$ so that the adjacency
of two vertices is a function (the *decoder*) of their two codes alone. The decoder may depend on
$\mathcal{F}$, but not on the individual graph $G$. The representation is *efficient* when the
codes have length $O(\log n)$. A family with an efficient implicit representation contains at
most $2^{O(n \log n)}$ labeled graphs on $n$ vertices, i.e. it has at most *factorial speed* of
growth. The implicit graph conjecture asserts the converse for hereditary families.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/implicit_graph_conjecture)
- [KNR92] Kannan, S., Naor, M. and Rudich, S., *Implicit representation of graphs*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992), 596–603.
- [Sp03] Spinrad, J. P., *Efficient graph representations*. Fields Institute Monographs 19,
  American Mathematical Society (2003).
- [HH22] Hatami, H. and Hatami, P., *The implicit graph conjecture is false*. FOCS 2022.
  [arXiv:2111.13198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13198)
-/

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/-- A family of finite labeled graphs: for each `n`, the set `F n` of members of the family
whose vertex set is `Fin n`. -/
abbrev GraphFamily := ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

/-- A graph family is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: for every
injection `σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n` and every `G ∈ F n`, the graph on `Fin m` in which `i` and `j`
are adjacent iff `σ i` and `σ j` are adjacent in `G` belongs to `F m`. Taking `m = n` shows
that a hereditary family is closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsHereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄ (σ : Fin m ↪ Fin n), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.comap σ ∈ F m

/-- A graph family has *at most factorial speed* of growth if it contains at most
$2^{O(n \log n)}$ graphs on the vertex set `Fin n`. -/
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)

/-- A graph family `F` has an *efficient implicit representation* if there are a constant `C`
and a decoder `D : {0,1}* × {0,1}* → Bool`, both depending only on `F`, such that every graph
`G ∈ F n` admits an assignment of binary codes of length at most `C * log n` to its vertices
with `D (code u) (code v) = true` iff `u` and `v` are adjacent in `G`, for all distinct
vertices `u`, `v`. The decoder is an arbitrary function; no computability is required. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℝ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Bool), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ F n,
    ∃ code : Fin n → List Bool,
      (∀ v, ((code v).length : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log n) ∧
        ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (G.Adj u v ↔ D (code u) (code v) = true)

/--
**The implicit graph conjecture** (asked as a question by Kannan, Naor and Rudich [KNR92] and
stated as a conjecture by Spinrad [Sp03]): every hereditary graph family with at most factorial
speed of growth, i.e. with at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$ labeled graphs on $n$ vertices, admits an
efficient implicit representation, i.e. an adjacency labeling scheme with $O(\log n)$-bit codes.

The conjecture is false: Hatami and Hatami [HH22] show that for every $\delta > 0$ there is a
hereditary graph family with at most factorial speed of growth all of whose implicit
representations need codes of length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 68]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ F : GraphFamily,
      IsHereditary F → HasAtMostFactorialSpeed F → HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by
  sorry

/-- The family of all finite graphs is hereditary. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isHereditary_univ : IsHereditary fun _ => Set.univ :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

/-- The family of edgeless graphs is hereditary. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isHereditary_bot : IsHereditary fun _ => {⊥} := by
  rintro m n σ G hG
  rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG ⊢
  subst hG
  rfl

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has at most factorial speed. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasAtMostFactorialSpeed_bot : HasAtMostFactorialSpeed fun _ => {⊥} :=
  ⟨0, fun n => by simp⟩

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has an efficient implicit representation: give every vertex
the empty code and let the decoder always answer `false`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasEfficientImplicitRepresentation_bot :
    HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation fun _ => {⊥} := by
  refine ⟨0, fun _ _ => false, fun n G hG => ⟨fun _ => [], fun v => by simp, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG
  subst hG
  simp

end ImplicitGraphConjecture

Graph families are families of labeled graphs on `Fin n`, as in the source (𝓕ₙ ⊆ graphs on [n]); hereditary is closure under `comap` along embeddings `Fin m ↪ Fin n`, which includes closure under isomorphism (m = n) exactly as the source notes.

Speed bound uses `Real.log` and a real constant C with a uniform `∀ n`; for n = 0, 1 the right side is 2^0 = 1 and `F n` has at most one element, so this equals the eventual big-O bound. Base of the logarithm is irrelevant under O().

namespace ImplicitGraphConjecture

/--
The implicit graph conjecture asks whether every hereditary family `F` of labeled finite
simple graphs with at most factorial speed has an efficient implicit representation.

Here heredity says that pulling a graph in `F n` back along any injection `Fin m ↪ Fin n`
produces a graph in `F m`; in particular, it includes closure under graph isomorphism. At most
factorial speed is the eventual bound $|F_n| \leq 2^{C n \log_2 n}$. An efficient implicit
representation consists of one decoder for the whole family and, for each graph in the family,
binary vertex labels of length at most $C'\log_2 n$ from which the decoder determines adjacency.
No computability condition is imposed on the decoder.

Hatami and Hatami refuted the conjecture, so the answer is false.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem implicit_graph_conjecture :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ F : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
        (∀ {m n : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}, G ∈ F n →
          ∀ f : Fin m ↪ Fin n, G.comap f ∈ F m) →
        (∃ growthConstant : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
          (F n).ncard ≤ 2 ^ (growthConstant * n * Nat.log 2 n)) →
        ∃ labelConstant : ℕ, ∃ decoder : List Bool → List Bool → Bool,
          ∀ {n : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}, G ∈ F n →
            ∃ label : Fin n → List Bool,
              (∀ v, (label v).length ≤ labelConstant * Nat.log 2 n) ∧
              ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ decoder (label u) (label v) = true := by
  sorry

end ImplicitGraphConjecture
